title: Kate Clanchy
gist: An author index page (not an article) for writer Kate Clanchy, listing just six Prospect pieces; the culture-and-fiction beat centres on the Lucy Letby case and assisted dying for the old — two contested UK institutional questions treated as cultural rather than legal stories.

themes.theme: Contested UK institutional cases in culture writing

insights.claim: Prospect runs the Lucy Letby case as a culture story arguing the conviction still needs to be talked about, showing continued elite-media appetite to reopen a settled UK criminal verdict.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Sustained media pressure on high-profile convictions is the precursor to formal review — relevant to UK institutional-trust and NHS scrutiny.
insights.quote: We need to talk about Lucy Letby
insights.locator: Culture / We need to talk about Lucy Letby

insights.claim: Assisted dying is being covered specifically through the lens of the old rather than the terminally ill, a framing that widens the policy question from end-of-life medicine to ageing itself.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: How assisted dying is framed shapes how far UK legislation extends — a policy variable for healthcare, insurance and pension liability modelling.
insights.quote: Go gentle: assisted dying and the old
insights.locator: Culture / Go gentle: assisted dying and the old

insights.claim: Prospect continues to publish original short fiction alongside its politics and ideas output, with this writer's six-item output including a short story and a fiction piece.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Maintaining a fiction slot is a differentiation cost some ideas magazines still pay for subscriber loyalty rather than traffic.
insights.locator: Fiction / The Not-Dead and the Saved
